title: Check whether your network traffic looks suspicious
subtitle: Upload a file with network data and get a real analysis in seconds — the model runs entirely in your browser, no data is sent to a server.

cache.checking: checking for a saved model in the browser…
cache.loaded: ✓ model loaded from local browser storage (IndexedDB) — training was not needed

training.title: Training the neural network
training.tooltip: The model is actually being trained in your browser — the estimated weight of every connection in the network is iteratively corrected across 25 passes through the training data (epochs).
training.archDesc: Dense(16, relu) → Dense(8, relu) → Dense(1, sigmoid) · Adam · binary crossentropy
training.placeholder: press "Start training" to see the live learning curve

results.title: Real results on the test set

roc.title: ROC curve
roc.tooltip: Shows the tradeoff between true positive rate (TPR) and false positive rate (FPR) across decision thresholds — computed live from the model's actual predictions. An AUC (area under the curve) closer to 1.0 means the model is better at telling normal and anomalous traffic apart, regardless of the chosen threshold.

livePred.title: Live prediction on a random sample
livePred.tooltip: A random flow is picked from the test set (which the model never saw during training), and what the model actually predicts at that moment is shown.
livePred.placeholder: press the button to try a real prediction from the model

importance.title: Feature importance (permutation importance)
importance.tooltip: For each feature, values are randomly shuffled across the test instances, and the drop in accuracy is measured — a larger drop means the model relied more heavily on that feature.
importance.desc: computed live by shuffling each column and measuring the accuracy drop

csv.title: Import your own CSV
csv.intro: Choose a file with network traffic data (CSV) — you'll get a result right away, no need to understand how the model works under the hood.
csv.disclaimer: The model was trained on a research dataset (ToN-IoT) and works best with similar network flow data. Results are for educational/demonstration purposes, not a substitute for a professional security system.
csv.tooltip: Upload a CSV file of network flows — the app recognizes both already-encoded columns and the Zeek naming convention (e.g. id.resp_p, orig_bytes, orig_pkts), which the ToN-IoT dataset itself is based on. The model will run a real prediction over your data in the browser.
csv.previewNote: This is how the app interpreted your columns before running the prediction — check that the values look right (e.g. proto_tcp/proto_udp shouldn't both be 0 if the flow is TCP or UDP traffic).
csv.zeekNote: Zeek-style column names are also automatically recognized (e.g. id.resp_p, orig_bytes, orig_pkts, resp_ip_bytes) — the same format used by the ToN-IoT dataset itself. Exact names aren't required, either convention works.

errors.empty: The file contains no data rows.
